newsitem.title: USA: NY green bond may pay for questionable items-paper.
newsitem.headline: NY green bond may pay for questionable items-paper.

text.p: New York State's proposed $1.75 billion bond act, which would raise funds to clean the state's air, water and land, was criticized for including questionable projects, the Albany Times Union said on Friday.
Change-NY, anti-tax lobbyists, cited parking facilities, zoos, employee salaries, urban cultural parks, aquariums, roads, golf courses and ski slopes as examples.

The Pataki Administration has not released a detailed list of the projects that the bond act would pay for, and none of them are guaranteed funding as the act gives state officials flexibility in spending the funds, the paper said.

A spokesman for Gov. George Pataki was quoted as saying that the proposed green bond will provide real environmental benefits. The act will be approved or rejected by the voters at the November 5 polls.
Further, the critics pointed out that $675 million has yet to be spent from the 1986 Environmental Quality Bond Act, which caused them to question whether some of the projects were emergencies.
